correctness_results: All 24 operation/status/error rows match the independently transcribed fixed case: six mutations, four expected errors, eleven replays, one rate denial and two read-only maintenance passes.
The complete canonical 12-row rate_before prefix is identical to rate_after rows 1-12. Resume, fixture, prefix and wait hashes are exact; final-state hashes chain correctly.

Four monotonic observer TIME receipts match the wait exactly and bind the resumed Redis run ID, fixture, entire prefix, robots START+8000 deadline and original lease. The final sample crosses the deadline before the suffix dispatch.

RATE12 returns the publicly reconstructible group-first RATE_BLOCKED reply with exact deadline and after_io=1. No pending/started reservations remained, global deadline was zero, group and origin deadlines were equal; no stricter tuple was being applied, so the observed unchanged state is correct.

RATE13 admits the document only after observed deadline crossing. RATE17 replays the already-started document reservation; RATE18 replays its START and RATE19 the historical robots START, all before the second deadline. RATE22 and RATE23 remain before that deadline too.

Independent formulas match all 33 initial counters and 2376 before/after/delta counter slots across the 24 rows. Starts and reservation creations never refund; delivery attempts increase only on the first START.

Global/group/origin effective intervals remain 0/8000/8000 and caps 2/1/1. Every rate updated_at, last_started_at and deadline projection matches the six mutations; no finish, replay, error, denial or maintenance shortens a deadline.

First-start record and document identity hashes are reconstructed from public fixture identity and protocol framing. Robots remains the first start; document history appears only at RATE16 and is unchanged by historical replays.

One claim/fence issues a 60000ms lease. Both reservation logical expiries remain its exact deadline, without renewal. Live reservation keys are persistent; finished keys expire at their respective FINISH times plus 86400000ms, unchanged on replay.

The state hash changes exactly six times, on the six intended mutations. All eighteen nonmutation rows retain the immediately preceding complete-state hash; rate_before final state matches RATE12 and rate_after final state matches RATE24.

Seven public response hashes are independently reconstructed: four errors, both BATCH_DONE replies with processed=3/more=0, and the group-first rate denial. Other full reply hashes are deliberately not reconstructed.
evidence_limitations: Opaque discarded owner/token/reservation identities, private fixture bytes and complete typed snapshots cannot be independently regenerated from the retained safe projection. Their full-state and fixture hashes are checked for binding/equality, not claimed to be recomputed from a reconstructed private state.

Seventeen full reply hashes include an opaque reservation ID and cannot be publicly reconstructed. START io_permission is not exported. Reviewed exact-reply producer checks support expected live=1/historical=0 semantics, but this review does not claim independent reconstruction of those reply bytes or the permission bit.

The initial suffix full snapshot across the wait is not separately exported; unchanged full state at suffix entry is supported by the reviewed producer assertion and successful phase receipt, not a new independent Redis read.

Row started_at_ms/finished_at_ms are observer Redis TIME brackets around ledger calls; successful now_ms is Lua Context.open TIME. Error rows correctly have null now_ms despite Lua internally reading TIME. The after-call bracket precedes the full snapshot; the final phase TIME includes the later checks.

Wait gaps 2784/2793/1832ms include stage overhead and are not sleep durations. The reviewed controller formula requests at most 2000/2000/1014ms from these samples; actual sleep duration is not retained. No equality-at-deadline live claim is made: crossing was +818ms and reservation +1793ms.

Controller action at_ms and invocation timestamps are host time. Retained snapshots/receipts are command-level observations, not internal Lua instruction/write traces, atomicity-under-crash proof or a crash cut of START/FINISH.

No independent origin-blocking, overlapping-worker/shared-concurrency, real HTTP/DNS, policy-tightening, performance, all-M4 or production activation claim is made. after_io=1 proves a recorded START on the fence, not network activity or response success.

Approval/CI/artifact provenance and documentation remain the main agent responsibility. Isolation, ACL denials, credential revocation, original action-journal integrity, resource absence and secret scanning remain the other reviewer responsibility and are not decided here.
